svg.title: Downunder Voices Cartoon of the Day — Wollondilly’s busiest B&B
svg.desc: Black-and-white pen-and-ink newspaper cartoon. On a farm in Wollondilly, south-west of Sydney, a weary fictional farmer in a bush hat and checked shirt stands on his lawn holding a clipboard covered in tally marks, pointing his pen as he counts deer and says: “…198, 199, 200. And the goats have booked the back paddock for Sunday.” Behind him a large herd of deer fills the paddock in front of hills and gum trees. A stag stands by the open farm gate next to a suitcase tagged 2 nights, under a sign reading No Vacancy; a doe eats the carrots in the vegie patch, a deer lies resting on the lawn and a spotted fawn wanders past. A weatherboard farmhouse with a verandah and water tank stands on the right. Caption: Wollondilly’s busiest B&B: 200 guests, not one booking.
svg.text: DOWNUNDER VOICES — CARTOON OF THE DAY

g.text: BOOKED THE BACK PADDOCK FOR SUNDAY.”

svg.text: WOLLONDILLY’S BUSIEST B&B: 200 GUESTS, NOT ONE BOOKING.
Source: ABC News, 18 November 2026 — Wollondilly Council seeks help with feral deer, pigs, goats and rabbits.
